content: The 2011 American Heart Association (AHA) and American Stroke Association (ASA) guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for the primary prevention of stroke. These guidelines emphasize the importance of addressing modifiable risk factors, such as hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, smoking, and physical inactivity, to reduce the incidence of first-time strokes. They also highlight the role of antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulation in specific high-risk populations, and lifestyle modifications in stroke prevention. The 2011 ASA/ACCF/AHA/AANN/AANS/ACR/ASNR/CNS/SAIP/SCAI/SIR/SNIS/SVM/SVS guideline focuses on the management of patients with extracranial carotid and vertebral artery disease. This document outlines diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, including imaging modalities for vascular assessment, medical management of atherosclerotic disease, and indications for revascularization procedures such as carotid endarterectomy or stenting. It also provides recommendations for the evaluation and treatment of asymptomatic and symptomatic patients with carotid artery stenosis. The section on carotid artery evaluation and revascularization before cardiac surgery addresses the assessment of carotid artery disease in patients undergoing cardiac procedures. It discusses the potential benefits and risks of preoperative carotid revascularization in individuals with significant stenosis and provides guidance on patient selection and timing of interventions to optimize outcomes.
